title: Passion Is Rare
coreMove: Test whether an interest is actually career-ready instead of treating any strong preference as a job map.
sourcePressure: Roadtrip Nation, Ira Glass, and the Canadian student statistic show messy paths and weak passion-to-work mapping.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reducing the point to never trust interests or pretending hobbies have no career signal.

sourceAnchors.name: Roadtrip Nation
sourceAnchors.detail: Official materials support a large archive of career stories and no single right path.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Roadtrip Nation matters because fulfilled people sound messier up close than their job titles suggest.

sourceAnchors.name: Ira Glass
sourceAnchors.detail: The official profile supports early weakness and long skill-building rather than instant certainty.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Ira Glass being bad for a long time is the useful detail, not the glamour of the finished voice.

sourceAnchors.name: The Canadian number
sourceAnchors.detail: Frozen secondary support reports that 84 of 100 students named passions, but only four of those 84 tied directly to work or education.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The Canadian number turns a vague hunch into a practical warning: most passions are not job maps.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence

exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer deciding whether loving podcasts means quitting for audio work
exampleSpecs.stakes: leaving stability before testing production under deadlines

exampleSpecs.audience: a senior choosing a major from club identity
exampleSpecs.stakes: choosing from identity instead of skill evidence

exampleSpecs.audience: a home baker considering culinary school after weekend sourdough
exampleSpecs.stakes: confusing eating, posting, and production stamina
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: compares Saturday pleasure with the third tray of identical test batches

exampleSpecs.audience: a retiree asked to turn family history passion into paid research
exampleSpecs.stakes: damaging a loved hobby by skipping the client skill test
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: uses two difficult client calls to separate loving ancestry from sourcing clean evidence for strangers
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a census page magnified on a monitor

exampleSpecs.audience: a climber reading mountain weekends as a career calling

skillTargets: separate hobby signal from occupational signal
use rarity as a planning constraint
read nonlinear career stories without forcing a calling

tryThisNowSpec: Write one interest, then add the exact paid role, skill, buyer, or institution it would need before becoming career evidence.
